units.title: Where AI helps from enquiry to renewal
units.moduleTitle: The customer journey and AI's role
units.goal: Distinguish AI preparation from human authority throughout a customer relationship.
units.practice: Write a three-sentence reply and a six-field handover. Label customer statements, product source, unknowns, contact status, next action and owner.

questions.prompt: For where ai helps from enquiry to renewal, which best next step follows the lesson's 'map the relationship' method?
options: An enquiry, application, issued policy and claim are different records.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
questions.explanation: An enquiry, application, issued policy and claim are different records. A new prospect enters discovery and registration. An existing policyholder can enter service or claims directly after appropriate verification. Do not force someone reporting a loss through a sales conversation or treat a registered enquiry as active cover.

units.title: Discovery without guessing
units.moduleTitle: The customer journey and AI's role
units.goal: Collect a useful needs record while keeping assumptions and unnecessary personal information out.
units.practice: Create five discovery questions for the shop owner. For each, state its purpose and how the answer changes the next action. Then write a record with known facts, stated-but-unverified facts and unknowns.

questions.prompt: For discovery without guessing, which best next step follows the lesson's 'begin with purpose' method?
options: Start by asking what the customer wants to understand or protect.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
questions.explanation: Start by asking what the customer wants to understand or protect. A broad question lets the person describe the need in their own words. Do not begin with a long form or a product recommendation. Explain why a follow-up fact is relevant before asking for it. Discovery should make the next conversation easier, not collect every detail that might someday be useful.

questions.prompt: For discovery without guessing, which best next step follows the lesson's 'ask in layers' method?
options: Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
Use an open question, a focused clarification and a short confirmation.
questions.explanation: Use an open question, a focused clarification and a short confirmation. For a business-owner enquiry, first ask what concern prompted the conversation, then clarify the activity relevant to that concern. Summarise the answer back for correction. Avoid leading questions that suggest a preferred response. Ask one clear question at a time when using messaging.

questions.prompt: For discovery without guessing, which best next step follows the lesson's 'label the evidence' method?
options: Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
A useful record distinguishes a customer statement, a verified document fact, an assumption and an unknown.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
questions.explanation: A useful record distinguishes a customer statement, a verified document fact, an assumption and an unknown. If a customer says they have existing cover, record it as stated until the applicable policy is checked. Do not silently promote a conversational answer into a verified product or eligibility fact. Include when the statement was made and the source of a verified fact.

questions.prompt: For discovery without guessing, which best next step follows the lesson's 'know when to refer' method?
options: Collect only information required for the immediate task under the organisation's approved process.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
questions.explanation: Collect only information required for the immediate task under the organisation's approved process. A customer may not know the answer or may prefer to discuss it with an officer. Record the gap and refer instead of guessing or pressuring. Do not place identity documents, financial details or health information into an unapproved AI tool simply to make the summary richer.

questions.prompt: In this unit's fictional case, what should a reviewer do before a customer-facing action?
options: Confirm the relevant source, facts, unknowns, contact status and responsible next action.
Assume the fictional example establishes the real customer's policy terms.
Treat a prepared message as proof it was delivered.
questions.explanation: A shop owner says, 'I need insurance for my business.' The assistant assumes the shop owns the building and drafts a building-cover explanation. The customer actually rents a stall and is worried about stock in transit. Correct the record by removing the unsupported ownership assumption. Ask which loss concerns them, what activity is involved and whether they want an officer to explain relevant options. The next officer receives the stated concern and the unanswered questions, not an invented business profile.

units.title: Product explanations grounded in approved sources
units.moduleTitle: The customer journey and AI's role
units.goal: Prepare a clear explanation that preserves the applicable product's meaning and limitations.
units.practice: Build a three-column evidence table: proposed statement, exact supporting passage, and review action. Include one benefit, one limitation and one unresolved question.

questions.prompt: For product explanations grounded in approved sources, which best next step follows the lesson's 'find the applicable source' method?
options: Check the insurer, product name, source owner, version and effective period before drafting.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
questions.explanation: Check the insurer, product name, source owner, version and effective period before drafting. Two similarly named products can have different terms. A marketing summary may omit conditions that appear in the wording. If sources conflict, mark the conflict and ask the authorised owner; do not combine whichever sentences make the offer sound strongest.

options: Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.

For each statement about a benefit, exclusion, condition or premium, identify the supporting passage in the applicable approved source.

A link to an entire folder is less useful than a specific document and passage. If support is absent, omit the claim or turn it into a referral question. AI-generated citations are suggestions until opened and checked.

questions.prompt: For product explanations grounded in approved sources, which best next step follows the lesson's 'simplify without changing meaning' method?
options: Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
Use short sentences and explain unfamiliar terms, but retain qualifications.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
questions.explanation: Use short sentences and explain unfamiliar terms, but retain qualifications. 'Subject to assessment' must not become 'will be paid'. A deductible or excess must not disappear from a benefit explanation. Present material limitations next to the relevant benefit so the customer does not receive an attractive headline and miss the condition elsewhere.

questions.prompt: In this unit's fictional case, what should a reviewer do before a customer-facing action?
options: Confirm the relevant source, facts, unknowns, contact status and responsible next action.
Assume the fictional example establishes the real customer's policy terms.

The customer-facing explanation should not invent a figure because the training extract does not supply one.

units.title: Lead qualification and prioritisation
units.goal: Choose the next follow-up using evidence without treating a worklist score as insurance eligibility.
units.practice: Create a worklist with evidence, missing facts, contact status, owner and next action. Explain why a priority is not an underwriting decision.

questions.prompt: For lead qualification and prioritisation, which best next step follows the lesson's 'define the next action' method?
options: Qualification asks whether there is enough relevant information and interest for a particular next step.
Treat a fluent draft as sufficient authority and proceed without checking the relevant record.
Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
questions.explanation: Qualification asks whether there is enough relevant information and interest for a particular next step. It is not a promise that an insurer will accept the customer. Define the action first: clarify a missing fact, explain an option or refer an application. A record can be ready for clarification while still being unready for an application.

units.title: Preparing a relevant outreach message
units.goal: Draft a useful, accurate invitation with an appropriate channel and a clear next step.
units.practice: Write a bounded drafting brief and a message of no more than seventy words. Mark the source, contact-status check, reviewer and intended next step separately from the customer message.

Replace missing facts with a plausible assumption so the worklist appears complete.
questions.explanation: Identify the intended audience and the single action the message should support. An invitation to ask about cover is different from an application request or a policy notice. Use only authorised audience inputs. Personalisation should be relevant and proportionate; avoid inserting sensitive or unexpected details just because a system can access them.

units.moduleTitle: Running and evaluating an AI-assisted workflow
units.goal: Prepare a bounded pilot that tests usefulness, review controls and customer outcomes before expansion.
units.practice: Prepare a one-page pilot plan with problem, scope, sources, roles, boundaries, test cases, metrics, stop conditions, review date and a continue/change/stop recommendation template.
